title: Efficient and Effective Edge-wise Graph Representation Learning

problem.claim: Existing graph representation learning methods primarily produce node representations and perform poorly in practical edge-wise applications because they neglect edge-specific properties and have inherent limitations.

gap.claim: Research on edge representation learning is scarce, and existing approaches either require high random-walk sampling costs or fail to capture high-order information between edges, compromising representation quality.

contributions.claim: TER generates edge representation vectors from graph structure surrounding edges and encodes high-order edge proximities into low-dimensional vectors.
AER generates edge representation vectors by augmenting edge attributes through a feature aggregation scheme.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The combined TER and AER edge representations achieved significantly superior edge-classification performance on 8 real-life datasets.
The combined representations were reported to be up to one order of magnitude faster than 16 baselines on large graphs.

narrative_sequence.summary: Graph representation learning is widely used for graph analysis because of its reported performance in real-world applications.
Most existing work focuses on node representations, while applying such methods to edges neglects edge-specific properties and performs poorly in practical edge-wise applications.
Edge representation learning remains underexplored, and existing methods face efficiency or high-order-information limitations.
The authors introduce TER for structure-based edge representations and AER for attribute-based edge representations.
The authors report improved edge-classification performance and substantial speed advantages over baselines.

source_observation.claim: The abstract separates edge representation signals into graph structure surrounding edges and edge attributes.

interpretation.claim: Different edge information sources may require complementary representation mechanisms.

application.claim: For edge-wise prediction tasks, consider combining structural proximity features with attribute-aggregation features.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that this combination is beneficial for tasks, graphs, or data regimes beyond the reported setting.

source_observation.claim: The reported approach targets both representation quality and computational efficiency.

interpretation.claim: Edge representation methods should evaluate predictive utility together with scalability.

application.claim: When comparing edge representation systems, measure both task performance and runtime on larger graphs.

exception.claim: The abstract does not provide runtime definitions, hardware details, or the conditions underlying the reported speedup.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the algorithms, objectives, or implementation details of TER and AER.

The identities and configurations of the 16 baselines are unspecified.
